s1.syndrome_frame: a gradually enlarging, red, cutaneous tumor with a hard nodule on the upper arm
salient_findings: red tumor on the right upper arm
key_facts: 16-year-old girl
previously healthy
lesion started as a small cutaneous nodule
enlarged over 6 months
no history of local trauma or insect bite
unremarkable personal, past, and family histories
6 × 6-cm protuberant, thick-walled, and well-defined red tumor
nontender, firm-to-hard nodule inside the tumor
normal laboratory tests
normal physical and systemic examinations
multilocular spaces below the epidermis on pathological examination
solid tumor in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance

shortlist.label: pilomatricoma
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical description of a gradually enlarging, red, cutaneous tumor with a hard nodule

shortlist.label: granular cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with a firm-to-hard nodule and cutaneous location

shortlist.label: schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of a firm, cutaneous nodule

shortlist.label: cutaneous leishmaniasis
shortlist.why_kept: can cause cutaneous lesions, although less likely given the clinical context

shortlist.label: bullous pilomatricoma
shortlist.why_kept: specific type of pilomatricoma that matches the bullous appearance described

raw.rationale: The presence of a firm-to-hard nodule inside the tumor, multilocular spaces below the epidermis, and a solid tumor in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance on pathological examination are characteristic of pilomatricoma. Additionally, the clinical presentation of a slowly enlarging, well-defined red tumor without regional lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms is consistent with pilomatricoma.

rejected.label: granular cell tumor
rejected.why: typically presents as a solitary, firm, and painless nodule, but the described pathological features do not match

rejected.label: schwannoma
rejected.why: usually presents as a well-circumscribed, firm, and sometimes tender mass, but the pathological features and clinical presentation do not align

rejected.label: cutaneous leishmaniasis
rejected.why: typically presents with a history of travel or exposure to endemic areas and ulcerative lesions, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: bullous pilomatricoma
rejected.why: a rare variant of pilomatricoma, but the described clinical and pathological features are more consistent with a typical pilomatricoma
